model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward: contracted ~3% escalators plus co-location/amendment leasing, net of Sprint (~$20M/yr to 2034) and normal churn; historical series not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are not meaningful: (1) FY2023-FY2025 are restated towers-only continuing operations while FY2022 and earlier include Fiber/small cells, so 3y/5y CAGRs span two different companies; (2) shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE since FY2024 (-$3,270M at Q2-26) after the $5.0B Fiber goodwill impairment and distributions in excess of earnings, so the equity CAGR is undefined; (3) GAAP EPS is impairment-dominated (FY2024 -$8.98). Continuing revenue fell 4,734 -> 4,264 (FY23-FY25, -5.1%/yr) on Sprint decommissioning and straight-line revenue roll-off; continuing SBC-adjusted FCF was flat (2,781 -> 2,802).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted continuing FCF CAGR (0.4%) is close to reported (0.0%): SBC is small (~2% of revenue) and falling in dollars, so no growing share of cash flow is being paid in stock.

scenario_narratives.base: Pure-play US tower REIT after the Fiber sale. With DISH/EchoStar's ~$220M already out of the FY2026 base, revenue returns to ~3.5% growth (≈3% escalators plus modest 5G densification amendments, less Sprint's ~$20M/yr) and glides to 2.5%. FY2027 AFFO steps up ~9% on the full-year interest saving from the ~$7B paydown and the last of the $65M cost programme, after which operating leverage is mostly consumed by refinancing old low-coupon debt. Leverage stays at 6.0-6.5x; no further buybacks modelled. Capitalised at a 9.5% cost of equity, this lands close to the market: the stock is pricing a steady tower annuity, not a recovery.
scenario_narratives.bull: The simplified tower story works: carrier densification (mid-band 5G, fixed-wireless load, AI-driven traffic) and a new-CEO turnkey-services push lift organic growth to ~4.5%, the cost base keeps shrinking, and refinancing is benign, so AFFO margin reaches ~55%. Satellite direct-to-device stays a rural niche. The multiple re-rates toward AMT/SBAC as churn clears (8.75% CoE, 3% terminal growth).
scenario_narratives.bear: Carrier consolidation and decommissioning keep churn elevated (further EchoStar/DISH exits, UScellular site rationalisation, AT&T/T-Mobile overlap), SpaceX/AST direct-to-device caps rural leasing and renewal pricing, and higher-for-longer rates reprice ~$2B/yr of debt at 6x+ leverage. Revenue grows 1-1.5%, AFFO margin erodes toward 49.5%, and the market prices CCI as an ex-growth, levered annuity (10.5% CoE, 1% terminal growth, 13x cap).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Crown Castle is valued on owner AFFO (company AFFO less SBC and net discretionary capex) capitalised at a cost of equity, because tower REIT cash flow is contracted rent after interest; net debt is never deducted a second time. The anchor is the July-2026 raised FY2026 guidance, the first clean towers-only year, with FY2027 lifted mechanically by the full-year interest saving from the Fiber-sale paydown. Historical CAGRs are unusable (restated continuing operations, negative equity, impairment-dominated EPS), so growth is built from escalators, leasing and churn.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are the large majority of site rental revenue; one MLA renegotiation moves the base case
EchoStar/DISH: ~$220M 2026 headwind plus litigation; any further default or termination is bear-case territory
Refinancing: ~$18.2B of debt at ~4.2% average cost reprices upward at 6.0-6.5x leverage; a 100bp higher refi rate is ~$180M of AFFO once fully rolled
Satellite direct-to-device (SpaceX/Starlink, AST SpaceMobile) as a long-duration substitute in low-density areas, compressing terminal growth
Cost-of-equity sensitivity: a terminal-heavy, low-growth annuity; each 50bp of CoE moves the base value by roughly 8-10%
AFFO includes non-cash prepaid-rent amortisation; if prepaid-rent receipts fall well below amortisation, owner cash flow is lower than modelled

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 66.84-100.50 (price sits at the bottom of the range)
data_sources.financials: CCI_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, continuing operations FY2023+) and SEC XBRL companyconcept API: EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 425,455,439 at 2026-08-03; InterestExpenseDebt Q1-26 $242M, Q2-26 $208M; ShareBasedCompensation FY25 $73M, H1-26 $47M; PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock H1-26 $1,017M; total debt $18,239M and cash $1,042M at 30-Jun-26
data_sources.qualitative: CCI_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): FY2026 guidance raised at Q2-26 (site rental revenue $3,833-3,878M, AFFO $1.95-2.00B, AFFO/share $4.53-4.65), dividend $1.0625/qtr, $65M cost programme, 6.0-6.5x leverage target, DISH/Sprint headwinds

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation: FY2025 $73M (10-K filed 2026-02-23), H1 FY2026 $47M (10-Q filed 2026-08-05); FY2026E ~$90M annualised (includes restructuring-related awards)
inputs.share_count_basis: 425.46M shares outstanding at 2026-08-03 (10-Q cover, filed 2026-08-05) plus ~1M unvested RSUs = 426.5M diluted; the ~$1.0B divestiture-funded buyback was executed in H1 2026 (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,017M YTD) and is already in this count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and no further buyback is assumed (leverage-neutral re-levering into buybacks is not modelled).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not WACC, because AFFO is already after interest. USD flows: US 10y ~4.4% + levered beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.4%, rounded to 9.5% base. Leverage (6.0-6.5x net debt/EBITDA target, ~6.2x at 30-Jun-26) and single-country, three-customer concentration are charged here once and not again in the flows. Bull 8.75% (re-rating to AMT/SBAC-like risk as churn clears), bear 10.5% (higher-for-longer refinancing at 6x+ leverage).
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground lease expense (tower land) is an operating cost already inside AFFO; no separate lease line. Land purchases that retire ground rent sit in discretionary capex (capex_pct_path).
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine with net_debt = 0 (dcf-methods routing row 'REIT / property trust'; first valuation of CCI, no prior model to match). AFFO is post-interest, so debt is NOT deducted again: reported net debt $17,197M (total debt $18,239M less cash $1,042M at 30-Jun-26, 10-Q) is recorded in reported_* fields only. Engine mapping: revenue = total revenue (site rental + services); ebitda_margin_path = AFFO / revenue (company-defined AFFO, which adds back SBC and deducts only sustaining capex); sbc_pct_path charges SBC back (owner basis); capex_pct_path = discretionary capex (augmentations, land purchases) net of customer prepaid-rent receipts, which AFFO does NOT deduct but which the growth path requires; also absorbs the non-cash prepaid-rent amortisation inside AFFO; da_pct and cash tax = 0 (REIT, cash taxes ~$15M/yr are inside AFFO). FY0 = FY2026E, anchored to the July-2026 raised guidance (Analysis.json guidance block; Q2-26 earnings): site rental revenue $3,833-3,878M + services ~$175M -> total ~$4,030M (H1-26 actual $2,018M x2); AFFO $1,950-2,000M (mid $1,975M, $4.53-4.65/share on ~430M weighted shares). FY2026 itself is a transition year (four months of pre-paydown interest, ~$240M DISH/Sprint churn already absorbed), so it is used as the base, not as a projection year; H2-26 retained cash after the $1.0625 quarterly dividend is immaterial. Year-1 (FY2027) AFFO margin 51.6% = FY26 $1,975M + ~$70M full-year interest saving (quarterly interest $242M Q1-26 -> $208M Q2-26 with two post-close months; run-rate ~$190M/qtr) + ~$20M remaining of the ~$65M cost programme + ~75% drop-through on ~$140M revenue growth - ~$20M refinancing drag. Divestiture: Fiber/small cells sold to EQT/Zayo for $8.5B, closed 1-May-26; FY2023+ rows in Metrics.csv are restated continuing (towers) operations, so pre-2023 history is a different company.

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin_path is AFFO/revenue (post-interest). Operating leverage on escalator revenue (~70-75% cash drop-through) is largely offset by refinancing ~$2B/yr of ~4.2%-average debt at ~5.3% (~$20-25M/yr drag) and ~3% ground-rent escalators, so the margin creeps up only ~1.2pp over the decade.
base.capex_note: Discretionary capex ~$180-190M/yr (continuing capex $182M FY25, $116M H1-26, less ~$35M sustaining already in AFFO), net of prepaid-rent receipts.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: revenue depends on three carriers plus a litigated EchoStar exposure, leverage is 6x+, and satellite direct-to-device is an unpriced long-duration threat. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs both faster leasing and a multiple re-rating under an unproven CEO. Base keeps 50% as the guidance-anchored, contracted-escalator path.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
